speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. Please describe your specific symptoms regarding the gait and limb ataxia you mentioned, and tell me how these issues began. Also, could you elaborate on your significant medical history?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: The description of appearing "drunk" while walking and feeling clumsy specifically on the right side suggests cerebellar ataxia. To determine the underlying cause, can you tell me if this clumsiness worsens when you try to touch your nose with your finger, and do you have any history of stroke, tumors, or head trauma? Additionally, have you noticed any changes in your speech or swallowing difficulties?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) secondary to natalizumab therapy. The combination of new-onset cerebellar ataxia and a history of Crohn's disease treated with natalizumab (an anti-CD52 monoclonal antibody) is highly suspicious for JC virus reactivation. I am requesting brain MRI images to confirm the presence of non-enhancing white matter lesions.
